journal_articles.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes.
journal_articles.abstract: Structural variants (SVs) are large (>50 base pairs) genomic rearrangements that can significantly influence human phenotypes, yet their contribution to health and disease remains undercharacterized. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of 1.6 million SVs identified in whole-genome sequencing data from 467,152 UK Biobank participants, across 13,322 binary, 2,018 quantitative, and 2,923 plasma protein traits. Of these, 82.25% of SVs were outside the detectable range of prior copy-number variant studies. Protein quantitative trait loci analysis linked 3,467 SVs to 1,690 proteins, with effects dependent on SV type and location. In SV-PheWAS, we detected 28,184 associations with human health outcomes. Notably, we uncovered rare SVs with strong phenotypic effects. Furthermore, we show that at known genome-wide association study loci, 32.21% of associated SVs overlapped functional genomic regions. This study underscores the underestimated role of SVs in human genetics and their potential to advance understanding of human biology and drug discovery.

journal_articles.title: A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants.
journal_articles.abstract: Trehalose-6-phosphate (T6P) is a central metabolic signal linking sugar availability to plant growth, carbon utilization, and productivity, yet its sensing and signaling mechanisms remain elusive. Using chemical biology and functional approaches, we identify the noncatalytic pseudoenzyme Class-II T6P synthase (TPS-II) as a T6P sensor in Arabidopsis. In the apo state, TPS-II dimerizes to form an autoinhibitory inter-subunit interaction. T6P binding to the N-terminal TPS-like domain triggers a conformational change that releases the C-terminal domain, enabling interaction with the central metabolic integrator SNF1-related protein kinase 1 (SnRK1) to repress its kinase activity. Loss of TPS-II genes activates catabolic and stress-responsive programs while suppressing anabolic gene expression, consistent with constitutive SnRK1 activity. Conservation of this T6P-TPS-II-SnRK1 signaling axis throughout the plant kingdom highlights its fundamental role in coupling carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis. These findings resolve a long-standing question in sugar signaling and provide a framework for improving crop carbon-use efficiency.

journal_articles.title: A telomere-to-telomere map of somatic mutation burden and functional impact in a cancer.
journal_articles.abstract: Cancer genomes harbor extensive somatic genetic and epigenetic variation, yet large portions of the genome remain inaccessible to conventional reference-based analyses. Here, we demonstrate that pairing a near-telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) diploid assembly of a donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of their melanoma reveals that 16% of somatic variants localize to sequences absent from GRCh38, with satellite repeats acting as hotspots for UV-associated mutagenesis. Centromere kinetochore binding domains emerge as focal sites of chromosome arm aneuploidy breakpoints and somatic genetic variation, features we further demonstrate are also present in non-cancerous tissues. By contrast, extensive epigenetic remodeling of kinetochore binding domains appears specific to oncogenesis. Single-molecule telomere analyses reconstruct the cycle of telomere erosion and telomerase-mediated extension during tumor evolution, while haplotype-resolved chromatin maps reveal widespread somatic epimutations impacting regulatory elements. Together, these findings define previously inaccessible dimensions of somatic variation and establish a framework for telomere-to-telomere studies of human mosaicism.

journal_articles.title: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia.
journal_articles.abstract: The mu-opioid receptor (MOR) is a major target for pain treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by dangerous side effects. However, the systemic administration of opioids makes it difficult both to decipher their underlying mechanisms of action and to limit drug action to specific receptor subpopulations to isolate therapeutic effects from adverse effects. Here, we develop a reversibly photoswitchable morphinan agonist termed "azo-morphine-3" (AM-3) that interconverts from low to high efficacy in response to light to enable optical control of MOR signaling. Structural analysis of the low ("trans") and high ("cis") efficacy states of AM-3 bound to the MOR reveals distinct binding modes, with each state driving unique ligand, receptor, and G protein dynamics. In mice, AM-3 drives reversible and repeatable optical control of antinociception across pain models with a reduced side effect profile owing to its limited brain accumulation and its ability to be locally activated.

journal_articles.title: Charting the silent variation within us.
journal_articles.abstract: Every cell in the human body carries its own genome, shaped by mutations acquired over a lifetime, yet this vast somatic variation has been nearly impossible to measure. The SMaHT Network now delivers benchmarked tools and the first body-wide map of somatic mosaicism, establishing a baseline of "normal" against which its roles in development, aging, and disease can finally be tested.

journal_articles.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing.
journal_articles.abstract: Coleoid cephalopods exhibit the highest levels of adenosine deaminases acting on RNA (ADAR)-mediated RNA editing of any known taxon, yet the functional consequences of most recoding events remain unclear. Here, we integrated proteomics with biochemical and cellular assays to characterize recoding across the Doryteuthis pealeii proteome. This confirmed the translation of 7,997 recoded sites at the protein level and revealed how recoding reshapes the proteome by altering protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modifications, and enzymatic activity. We find that recoding also creates or ablates post-translational modification sites, with direct effects on protein function and protein-protein interactions. Recoding the E3 ligase MARCHF5 drives widespread changes in substrate ubiquitylation and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, illustrating how RNA editing can influence organelle function. Together, these data give a proteome-scale view of how extensive RNA recoding diversifies protein function in coleoid cephalopods and offer a framework for understanding how RNA-level plasticity shapes protein function and cellular physiology.

journal_articles.title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression.
journal_articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is implicated as a vulnerability in multiple cancers, yet approaches for effectively inducing ferroptosis in vivo are limited. Bypassing conventional strategies targeting the antiferroptotic glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) proteins, we designed metabolic initiators of lipid peroxidation (MILPOs) and developed the compounds WMK-1/2, which contain tetraoxane radical-generating and mitochondria-targeting groups, as de novo ferroptosis inducers. WMK-1 localizes primarily to mitochondria, induces local lipid peroxidation, and impairs oxidative phosphorylation. WMK-1 induces a "mito-ferroptosis" sub-pathway that skips GPX4 inhibition as a prerequisite, can be rescued by lipophilic radical-trapping antioxidants, yet is minimally sensitive to acyl-coenzyme A synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) perturbation and long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) supplementation, and evades retinol-mediated protection. Instead, WMK-1-induced cell death requires labile Fe2+ and can be selectively suppressed by ɑ-lipoic acid, an endogenous, mitochondria-resident antioxidant. WMK-1/2 are bioavailable and exhibit significant efficacy in tumor suppression by eliciting ferroptosis in multiple cancer models and augmenting the antitumor effects of immune-checkpoint blockers. Our work provides a protein-targeting-independent metabolic ferroptosis induction strategy for potential cancer therapy.

journal_articles.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system.
journal_articles.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin (TeNT) invades the central nervous system (CNS) via retrograde transport through motoneurons. Whether a host factor is needed to mediate TeNT trafficking has remained unknown. Here, using pull-down and mass spectrometry analysis, and by developing a luciferase-based in vivo transport assay, we identify receptor protein tyrosine phosphatase sigma (PTPRS; PTPσ) as the retrograde transport receptor for TeNT. Global or motoneuron-specific PTPRS knockout (KO) abolishes TeNT entry into the CNS in mouse models. PTPRS-TeNT interactions occur in endosomes, prevent toxin translocation, and direct TeNT trafficking in neurons. Structural studies establish that the TeNT light chain and belt region bind to the immunoglobulin domain of PTPRS. Disrupting TeNT-PTPRS interactions blocks TeNT trafficking into the spinal cord; consistently, a PTPRS-binding-deficient TeNT mutant induces botulism-like flaccid paralysis. Thus, PTPRS is the host factor mediating TeNT trafficking into the CNS, revealing a targetable pathway for post-entry intervention and drug delivery into the CNS.

journal_articles.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations.
journal_articles.abstract: Human centromeres are highly variable but remain among the least characterized regions of the genome because their repetitive structure has hindered conventional analysis of population diversity and disease relevance. Here, we show that rare k-mers in centromeric regions capture lineage-specific variation, defining discrete haplogroups with distinct structural features. We developed ascairn to infer these haplogroups from short-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. Applying this framework to >3,300 genomes reveals extensive global diversity in centromere haplogroups and signatures of population history. Analyzing short-read WGS data from 142 oligodendroglioma cases with 1p/19q co-deletion, we mapped breakpoints to the centromere regions of chromosomes 1 and 19, revealing a clear positional relationship to kinetochore attachment sites and a link between centromere haplotype structure and rearrangement susceptibility. Rare k-mers thus open centromeres to population-scale analysis, linking centromere structural diversity to human evolutionary history and disease-associated genomic instability.

journal_articles.title: Aberrant recursive splicing in a human disease locus.
journal_articles.abstract: Recursive splice sites are rare motifs postulated to facilitate splicing across massive introns and shape isoform diversity. The necessity of recursive splicing (RS) and its role in human disease are unsubstantiated. Here, we use CRISPR to model intronic deletions eliminating an RS site (RS1) in CADM2 and conferring risk for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and other neurobehavioral traits. Ablating RS1 in human induced neurons alters the gradient of RNA abundance across CADM2's first intron, decreases CADM2 expression, and impacts transcript usage. Decreased CADM2 expression is reflected in reduced exon usage downstream of RS1 and global alteration to genes involved in neuronal processes. In vivo rodent models harboring Cadm2 RS1 deletions exhibit an attenuated effect on Cadm2 expression and modest changes in behavior and functional brain connectivity. This study demonstrates RS as a noncoding regulatory mechanism in a gene associated with a spectrum of neuropsychiatric and behavioral traits.

journal_articles.title: Anterior cingulate feedback facilitates rapid global context modulation in primary visual cortex.
journal_articles.abstract: Context modulates sensory processing. Recent proposals claim early areas like primary visual cortex (V1) are only influenced by "local" context (e.g., recent stimulus history), while "global" context (e.g., learned patterns and probabilities) modulates only higher areas. We tested this using a global/local oddball paradigm: mice viewed repeating five-item sequences (AAAA-B), where B is deviant from local context but typical in global context. Using two-photon imaging and local field potential (LFP) recording in mouse V1, we found that global predictability normalized responses to B stimuli. This effect emerged after fewer than 10 sequence repetitions, demonstrating rapid learning. When a globally deviant "C" stimulus replaced B or when B occurred at unpredictable intervals (i.e., standard oddball), V1 showed strong response enhancement. This global context modulation in V1 required top-down feedback from anterior cingulate area. However, when B was replaced by an A (AAAA-A), responses were mixed, suggesting that stimulus-specific adaptation can constrain prediction-error signals in V1.

journal_articles.title: Cingulate thrombospondin 4 protects against neuropathic pain and comorbid anxiodepression via interaction with EAAT2.
journal_articles.abstract: Patients with neuropathic pain frequently present with emotional disorders. Cellular plasticity within anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is considered as a key interface linking pain and emotion. However, mounting efforts have been devoted to elucidating intracellular mechanisms of plasticity, how extracellular alterations trigger intracellular changes remains elusive. Thrombospondin (THBS), a key component of extracellular matrix (ECM), is involved in various pathophysiological processes. Here, we show that THBS4 is downregulated in the ACC following peripheral neuropathy. Overexpressing cingulate THBS4 alleviates pain hypersensitivity and anxiodepression. Mechanistic analysis indicates that THBS4 maintains glutamate homeostasis via direct regulation of excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2) in astrocytic membrane, further stabilizing abnormal plasticity of pyramidal neurons and eventually producing analgesic, anxiolytic, and antidepressive effects. Taken together, we show THBS4-mediated neuron-astrocyte crosstalk as a key mechanism underlying neuropathic pain and comorbid anxiodepression. Recombinant THBS4 protein represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treatment of neuropathic pain and anxiodepression.

journal_articles.title: Deciphering genomic adaptations and climate resilience in the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica.
journal_articles.abstract: Seagrasses are coastal foundation species that support ecosystem stability but face increasing global change. Here, we assemble a chromosome-level reference genome for the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica to investigate adaptive evolution and climate resilience. Comparative genomic analyses reveal features underlying intertidal adaptation, including ion transport, circadian regulation, and stress responses. We identify positively selected genes associated with the transition to marine environments. Population genomic analyses identify strong divergence between northern and southern populations, reflecting deep historical separation, largely independent evolutionary trajectories, and local adaptation. Selection signals are enriched in stress response and ion transport genes, among which TIP3-1 confers tolerance to both salinity and heat. Genomic offset projections indicate greater climate vulnerability in northern populations, whereas southern populations show higher adaptive potential and may serve as genetic sources for assisted gene flow. Together, our study provides a genomic framework for understanding adaptation and guiding conservation under climate change.

journal_articles.title: Dopamine-induced mitochondrial dysfunction activates cGAS-sTING to drive IL-6 secretion in macrophages.
journal_articles.abstract: Despite growing evidence that dopamine acts as an innate immune inflammatory mediator, the molecular mechanisms by which dopamine modulates human immune function are incompletely defined. Here, we define the pathway in which dopamine induces robust IL-6 secretion in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages (hMDMs) through mitochondrial stress. Dopamine initiates a transient mitochondrial membrane depolarization that leads to sustained alterations in mitochondrial dynamics, including morphology and metabolism. These events promote the release of mtDNA into the cytoplasm, triggering the cGAS-STING pathway and NF-κB signaling. Pharmacological inhibition at multiple nodes of this pathway attenuates IL-6 secretion, establishing mitochondrial dysfunction and cGAS-STING signaling as central mediators of dopamine-driven IL-6 secretion. Variability in dopamine receptor expression across donors correlates with the magnitude of IL-6 responses. These findings highlight a potential link between dopamine signaling and systemic inflammation and suggest that differences in dopamine receptor expression may contribute to inter-individual variation in innate immune responses.

journal_articles.title: EpCAM-dependent membrane mechanics regulate nuclear deformation and promote gastric cancer metastasis.
journal_articles.abstract: Diffuse gastric cancer is highly metastatic and lacks effective therapeutic targets. Using membrane proteomics, gastric cancer cell models, biophysical measurements, and in vivo metastasis assays, we identify EpCAM as a regulator of membrane-cytoskeletal mechanics. EpCAM overexpression was associated with reduced apparent plasma membrane tension, ERM-actin remodeling, increased traction forces, and nuclear deformation. Functional perturbation of ezrin and lamin A/C supported the involvement of membrane-cytoskeleton-nucleus mechanical coupling in confined migration. EpCAM knockout or monoclonal antibody blockade reduced tumor invasion and lymph node dissemination in vivo. These findings establish a mechanobiological framework linking EpCAM-dependent membrane mechanics to metastatic behavior and highlight EpCAM-associated mechanical regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in diffuse gastric cancer.

journal_articles.title: Genomic insights into millennia of genetic continuity and trans-regional admixture in the middle-lower Yellow River basin.
journal_articles.abstract: The middle and lower Yellow River regions were crucial for early agricultural development and the emergence of complex societies in East Asia, yet their fine-scale population history from the Neolithic to historical periods remains incompletely resolved. Here, we present genome-wide data from 61 ancient individuals (∼4,500-200 before present [BP]) from Henan and Shandong. Our analyses show that middle-to-late Neolithic populations at Dahecun in Henan are genetically homogeneous and closely related to contemporaneous Yellow River millet-farming populations. By ∼3,000 BP, Shandong populations shift toward a late Neolithic middle Yellow River-related ancestry profile, consistent with the eastward expansion of middle Yellow River agricultural populations. This ancestry profile persists into historical periods, indicating long-term genetic continuity in Shandong. Two Tang-Song-period individuals from western Shandong carry ∼15% West Eurasian-related ancestry, indicating limited cross-regional genetic interaction. These findings refine the population history of the middle and lower Yellow River regions.

journal_articles.title: Human organ chip models recapitulate FRC-driven high endothelial venule differentiation, immune recruitment, and cancer-induced disruption.
journal_articles.abstract: High endothelial venules (HEVs) are specialized post-capillary venules that gate lymphocyte entry into lymph nodes, yet human in vitro models that capture their specialization remain limited. Here, we develop a perfusable human HEV-on-chip in which blood endothelial cells (BECs) form an engineered microvessel within a collagen-fibrin matrix populated by human fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs). The presence of FRCs, without exogenous LIGHT, drives HEV-associated marker expression (PNAd/MECA-79 and VCAM-1) and a plump endothelial wall enwrapped by a thickened laminin+ basement membrane, recapitulating features of lymph-node HEVs. Functionally, HEV-like vessels support markedly increased T-lymphocyte adhesion while preserving VE-cadherin junctions. Introducing MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells in an adjacent channel reduces MECA-79, disrupts junctional organization, and increases permeability without inducing apoptosis. Together, this platform defines a stromal instruction program for human HEV identity and a tractable model of cancer-associated HEV dysfunction.

journal_articles.title: ICAM-1 functions as a functional receptor for encephalomyocarditis virus and reveals a compensatory interplay with ICAM-4.
journal_articles.abstract: Encephalomyocarditis virus (EMCV) is the most widespread zoonotic pathogen that causes piglet death. EMCV enters cells via caveolin-mediated endocytosis. However, the receptors required for EMCV entry into the cells are unknown. Here, we show that intercellular cell adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) serves as a significant functional receptor during adsorption and entry. ICAM-1 binds directly to the EMCV viral proteins VP1 and VP2 with high affinity. Consistently, a soluble ICAM-1 fusion protein or anti-ICAM-1 blocking antibody impairs EMCV infection in susceptible human and mouse cells. Domain 1 of ICAM-1 is involved in the recognition of EMCV. ICAM-4 serves as a receptor in ICAM-1 knockout/knockdown mice and cell lines during EMCV infection. These findings suggest that ICAM-1 and ICAM-4 are entry receptors for EMCV and that targeting ICAM-1 D1 could be a potential strategy for the development of antivirals against EMCV.

journal_articles.title: Inhibiting the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex selectively enhances unsupervised statistical learning.
journal_articles.abstract: The brain must balance the automatic extraction of regularities with top-down cognitive control, yet the hemispheric contributions of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) remain unresolved. Here, we applied inhibitory repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation to the left, right, or bilateral DLPFC in 95 adults during a probabilistic sequence learning task. We found that inhibiting the right and bilateral DLPFC enhanced statistical learning compared to sham stimulation. Contrary to the hypothesis that interference from existing knowledge would mediate this effect, episodic memory performance was unaffected. As an alternative, we propose that right DLPFC inhibition shifts cognitive processing toward an exploratory information-sampling strategy, supported by our finding of greater reaction time variability in the right and bilateral stimulation groups. Our results provide causal evidence for a right-lateralized suppressive influence of the DLPFC on unsupervised learning and suggest that its role is linked to information-processing style rather than direct competition with episodic memory systems.

journal_articles.title: Lipid droplet targeting drives substrate access during very long chain fatty acid activation by Fat1.
journal_articles.abstract: Fatty acids require conjugation with coenzyme A (CoA) for their incorporation into membrane lipids. Of these, very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs), the precursors of yeast ceramides, are particularly hydrophobic. Yet, it remains unresolved where and how the sole VLCFA-CoA synthetase Fat1 activates them. Here, we show that lipid droplets (LDs) are both the site of free VLCFA storage and their place of activation. Free VLCFAs preferentially partition into LDs in molecular simulations and in vitro reconstitutions, whereas Fat1 targets the LD surface in cells via an N-terminal amphipathic helix. Structural predictions identify an essential hydrophobic cavity in Fat1 that connects the active site to the membrane, suggesting that VLCFAs shuttle directly from the LD core into the enzymatic pocket. Our model explains how the organelle targeting of a fatty acid activator evolved to match the biophysical properties, and consequently, the subcellular localization of its highly hydrophobic substrate.

journal_articles.title: Macrophage-induced ferritin expression protects pancreatic cancer cells from ferroptosis.
journal_articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) drive pro-tumorigenic signaling but also promote lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, making ROS regulation critical during high oxidative stress stages of tumor progression, such as metastasis. Loss of the antioxidant TIGAR in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells raises ROS and enhances metastatic behavior but also sensitizes cells to ferroptosis. To understand how TIGAR-null cells survive to metastasize, we examine the role of macrophage infiltration, which is increased in TIGAR-null tumors. Co-culturing TIGAR-null PDAC cells with macrophages protects them from ferroptosis. The tumor cells induce macrophage IL-6 secretion, which leads to the activation of STAT3 and upregulation of the iron-sequestering protein ferritin (FTH1) in cancer cells. FTH1 depletion in TIGAR-null cells restores ferroptosis sensitivity and reduces lung metastasis. These results suggest that the outcome of increased ROS in tumors may depend on the activation of mechanisms that selectively prevent ferroptosis while preserving ROS-induced oncogenic signaling and metastasis-promoting pathways.

journal_articles.title: Meningeal inflammation and arachnoid barrier breakdown in a mouse model of neonatal bacterial meningitis.
journal_articles.abstract: Newborns are especially susceptible to bacterial meningitis, primarily caused by group B Streptococcus (GBS), due to incomplete maturation of immune and barrier systems. While meningitis is well known to break down the blood-brain barrier, its effect on the meningeal arachnoid barrier remains poorly understood. Using a neonatal bacterial meningitis model, we demonstrate that GBS infection significantly increases arachnoid barrier permeability, disrupts tight junctions, and elevates meningeal production of proinflammatory cytokines. CD206+/LYVE-1+ border-associated macrophages undergo morphological and molecular activation post-infection, but their depletion prior to infection does not attenuate arachnoid barrier leakage or cytokine levels. We show that meningeal fibroblasts are a source of proinflammatory cytokines in response to GBS infection and that a systemic exposure of TNF-α alone is sufficient to induce barrier breakdown. These results support that the neonatal arachnoid barrier is vulnerable to cytokine-induced breakdown and highlight the role of non-immune meningeal cells like fibroblasts during bacterial infection.

journal_articles.title: Molecular mechanisms of promoter silencing by transcriptional readthrough.
journal_articles.abstract: Transcriptional interference is the in cis suppression of one transcriptional process by another. To define the mechanisms by which transcriptional readthrough is converted into stable gene silencing, we develop a mouse cell line model of cobalamin C deficiency associated with MMACHC silencing (epi-cblC) by deleting the Prdx1 intron 5 splice acceptor, thereby inducing antisense transcription across Mmachc. Readthrough results in ectopic H3K36me3 deposition, de novo DNA methylation, and stable silencing of Mmachc. Through systematic perturbations of transcription and the H3K36 and DNA methylation machinery, we demonstrate that antisense transcription is the primary driver of repression, whereas H3K36me3 contributes directly to promoter silencing and is further required for the establishment of DNA methylation, which in turn confers long-term stability. Together, these findings define a hierarchical silencing cascade by which transcriptional readthrough establishes stable gene repression and demonstrate that transcription itself can direct local chromatin remodeling and changes in gene expression.

journal_articles.title: NONO mitigates transcription-replication conflicts during replication stress by restraining BRD4-dependent transcription elongation.
journal_articles.abstract: Transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) drive genomic instability and are linked to tumorigenesis and treatment response. Replication stress exacerbates TRCs, but how cells coordinate transcription and replication to limit these conflicts remains unclear. Here, we identify NONO as a key regulator that maintains transcription-replication balance via BRD4 under replication stress. Replication stress triggers NONO acetylation at K243, enhancing BRD4 binding. On single-stranded DNA, NONO-BRD4 form condensates that block paused RNA polymerase II (RNAP2) release, fine-tuning elongation. NONO loss causes aberrant accumulation of elongating RNAP2 at termination regions, promoting TRCs and genomic instability. Conditions that increase origin firing, including ATR inhibition or BRCA2 deficiency, further exacerbate this phenotype in NONO-deficient cells, leading to pronounced synthetic lethality. Together, these findings define a NONO-mediated surveillance mechanism that couples replication stress to transcriptional restraint via condensate-dependent regulation of BRD4, and identify NONO as a potential therapeutic target in replication stress-driven cancers.

journal_articles.title: Peptide signaling in the paraventricular thalamus is essential for disrupted adult reward behaviors consequent to early-life adversity.
journal_articles.abstract: Early-life adversity (ELA) is strongly linked to emotional disorders characterized by dysregulated reward behaviors. However, the mechanisms by which transient neonatal experiences generate enduring, sex-specific alterations in brain function remain unresolved. Paraventricular thalamus (PVT) neurons are selectively activated during ELA and contribute to disrupted adult reward behaviors. Here, we explore the molecular mechanisms behind these enduring, sex-specific disruptions. Combining activity-dependent genetic labeling with translating ribosome affinity purification, we find distinct gene translation programs in ELA and control mice of both sexes. Notably, the receptor for the neuropeptide corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor type 1 (Crhr1), is differentially expressed across rearing and sex in response to reward. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated Crhr1 deletion exclusively in early-life-activated PVT neurons normalizes reward behaviors in both male and female adult ELA mice. Thus, CRHR1 signaling in adult PVT neurons activated by ELA is a required and potentially targetable mechanism underlying sex-specific, ELA-induced disruptions of reward behaviors.

journal_articles.title: Pharmacologically targeting CDK12 induces BRCAness and synergizes with merestinib to exacerbate DNA damage in high-risk neuroblastoma.
journal_articles.abstract: High-risk neuroblastoma remains a leading cause of pediatric cancer mortality, underscoring the need for novel therapeutics. MYCN amplification drives transcriptional addiction, creating vulnerabilities for therapeutic intervention. Inhibition of CDK12, a key regulator of transcription elongation, downregulates DNA damage response (DDR) genes. CDK12 inactivation using protein degraders and small molecules, including the orally bioavailable, selective CDK12/13 inhibitor OKI-1546, induced BRCAness and apoptosis in neuroblastoma cells. High-throughput compound screening combined with CDK12 inhibition/degradation revealed synergistic interactions encompassing multiple biological pathways. Merestinib, a multi-kinase inhibitor, emerged as the top synergistic agent across a panel of neuroblastoma in vitro models. Combining OKI-1546 with merestinib amplified DDR downregulation and diminished MYCN-driven signaling. OKI-1546 treatment reduced tumor growth and extended survival in vivo, which was enhanced when combined with merestinib. Whilst further in vivo validation is warranted, our findings nominate CDK12 as a promising therapeutic target in high-risk neuroblastoma, which can be exploited through combinatorial treatments.

journal_articles.title: Spatial distribution of blood-brain barrier membrane proteins is controlled by sorting motifs and physiological signals in vivo.
journal_articles.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB), formed by brain endothelial cells (BECs), creates a safe and homeostatic environment for proper brain function. While BECs are extraordinarily thin, their luminal and abluminal plasma membranes face markedly different environments: the blood and brain parenchyma, respectively. How BBB membrane proteins are spatially distributed between these membranes and the factors regulating their localization are not clear. Here, we establish a method for measuring polarized protein sorting at the BBB in vivo. We characterize the distribution of transporters and receptors on the luminal and abluminal plasma membranes and identify protein-intrinsic motifs that control polarized sorting. Finally, we observe a change in membrane protein distribution that aligns with circadian rhythms, revealing an under-appreciated dimension of BBB dynamics. This method can be broadly used for evaluating membrane protein landscape changes during development and disease and for choosing optimal molecular targets for BBB-crossing therapeutics.

journal_articles.title: Structural basis for cross-alphaherpesvirus neutralization by an antibody targeting a conserved hotspot on glycoprotein B.
journal_articles.abstract: Alphaherpesviruses, including herpes simplex viruses (HSV-1/2) and pseudorabies virus (PRV), pose significant threats to human and animal health, yet broad-spectrum interventions remain elusive. Here, we characterize C12A6, a neutralizing antibody (nAb) targeting glycoprotein B (gB) that cross-neutralizes HSV-1, HSV-2, and PRV and confers substantial, although incomplete, therapeutic protection against lethal HSV-1 or PRV infection. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of C12A6 in complex with PRV gB and HSV-2 gB reveal that the antibody engages a conserved conformational epitope on Domain I (DI). A conserved interaction framework, anchored by invariant polar contacts and a hydrophobic core, supports recognition across divergent alphaherpesvirus gBs. Comparison with the broader alphaherpesvirus antibody 16F9 shows that C12A6 additionally engages less-conserved peripheral residues, providing a structural basis for its more restricted recognition breadth. These findings define the structural basis for C12A6-mediated cross-neutralization and illuminate the functional architecture of gB DI as a target for broad-spectrum antiviral development.

journal_articles.title: TDP2-mediated DNA repair regulates the dynamics of neuronal early response gene transcription and cortical neuron connectivity.
journal_articles.abstract: Neuronal activity induces topoisomerase IIβ (TOP2B) to form DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within the promoters of early response genes (ERGs), such as Fos and Npas4, and facilitates rapid ERG transcription. However, the mechanisms that repair activity-induced DSBs and their significance for neuronal function remain ill-defined. Here, we report that depletion of tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase 2 (TDP2) in cultured mouse cortical neurons delays the repair of TOP2B-mediated DSBs and prolongs ERG expression following neuronal stimulation. Deleting Tdp2 in excitatory forebrain neurons in vivo caused DSB accrual, ERG overexpression, and increased excitatory synaptic transmission and cortical circuit dysfunction. Whereas proliferating cells utilize alternative pathways to process TOP2B-mediated DSBs, we find that such mechanisms are relatively inactive in postmitotic neurons. Overall, these results indicate that TDP2-mediated DNA repair is crucial for the temporal control of ERG transcription and suggest that defective repair of activity-induced DSBs could underlie neurological abnormalities in individuals with TDP2 mutations.

journal_articles.title: TM6SF2 acts at ER membrane contact sites to enable RAB7-dependent endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintain Golgi structure.
journal_articles.abstract: Although a loss-of-function variant of TM6SF2 is a highly penetrant risk factor for steatotic liver disease, including progression to cirrhosis and cancer, its normal function is largely unknown. Here we show that endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-localized TM6SF2 forms membrane contact sites (MCSs) with late endosomes/lysosomes, where it activates the small GTPase RAB7 to enable an endolysosomal route for selective secretion of lipid-rich very low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) particles. In accord, TM6SF2 and RAB7 deficiency similarly cause endolysosomal VLDL retention and accumulation of enlarged late endosomes/lysosomes. TM6SF2 further binds to VAMP-associated protein (VAP) ER-anchor proteins to maintain MCSs between the ER, endosomes, and the trans-Golgi network, with TM6SF2 deficiency causing Golgi fragmentation and disruption of cGAS-STING signaling known to prevent cirrhosis and cancer by clearing senescent hepatocytes. Our findings establish TM6SF2 as an ER-MCS component that enables endolysosomal VLDL secretion and maintains Golgi structure, which suggests that TM6SF2 loss of function causes liver disease through steatosis-dependent and independent mechanisms.

journal_articles.title: The NuRD complex shapes RNA polymerase III activity at highly expressed tRNA gene clusters, tuning the dynamic range of cellular tRNA pools.
journal_articles.abstract: RNA polymerase III (Pol III) transcription produces RNAs involved in core biological processes and is therefore coupled to fluctuating demands for protein synthesis and cell growth. However, the mechanisms underlying dynamic Pol III regulation remain incompletely understood. To address this gap, we investigated protein-protein interactions shared across multiple Pol III subunits to characterize the macromolecular interactome of Pol III, with special attention directed toward potential regulatory factors. Our survey uncovers interactions between Pol III and the NuRD (nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase) complex. We further show that NuRD localizes to active Pol III-transcribed genes, including tRNA gene clusters associated with notably high expression. Inhibiting NuRD-associated deacetylase activity increases Pol III transcription at these sites, suggesting that NuRD constrains Pol III activity and thereby modulates the dynamic range of Pol III-derived RNAs. These findings implicate NuRD as a chromatin-based mechanism linking signaling events and metabolic need with the dynamic availability of specific tRNA pools.

journal_articles.title: USP9X promotes the degradation of trapped translation factors on collided ribosomes.
journal_articles.abstract: Various ribosome-associated quality control pathways safeguard translation fidelity by detecting and resolving aberrant translation events. Recently, a pathway that senses stalled ribosomes with an occluded A-site has been described. The small molecules NVS1.1 and ternatin-4 induce ribosome stalling by trapping eukaryotic release factor 1 (eRF1) and elongation factor 1A1 (eEF1A1), respectively, within the ribosomal A-site, thereby promoting their ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Additionally to the previously identified factors GCN1, RNF14, and RNF25, we identify here the deubiquitinase USP9X as a regulator of this pathway. In the absence of USP9X deubiquitinase activity, eRF1 is still ubiquitinated but fails to undergo efficient degradation. However, compared with wild-type cells, K6-linked ubiquitin chains accumulate on eRF1 in cells lacking USP9X activity, suggesting that USP9X trims K6-linked ubiquitin chains during a late step of substrate processing. Furthermore, clearance of trapped eRF1 engages a feedback mechanism involving 4EHP and the integrated stress response (ISR) to suppress translation, whereas impaired degradation prevents translational shutdown.

journal_articles.title: Untranslated region rewiring defines a novel class of oncogene fusions.
journal_articles.abstract: Gene fusions in cancer are traditionally understood to generate hybrid proteins with altered functions that promote malignancy. Here, we define a previously unrecognized class of oncogenic fusions that preserve protein structure but replace the 5' untranslated region (5' UTR), thereby rewiring translational regulation. Using the MET oncogene as a paradigm, we show that 5' UTR-replacing fusions, identified across >200,000 cancer samples, increase MET protein abundance 5- to 10-fold without corresponding changes in mRNA levels. The resulting receptor remains correctly localized, ligand-responsive, and active, thereby promoting cell survival and motility. These fusion transcripts are detected following irradiation, documenting UTR rewiring in a post-treatment context. Beyond MET, similar 5' UTR-replacing fusions occur in FGFR1, JAK2, and NTRK2, where partner-derived 5 'UTRs are associated with reduced regulatory complexity and enhanced protein output. Together, our findings establish UTR rewiring as an overlooked mechanism of oncogene overexpression with implications for cancer genome annotation and precision oncology.

journal_articles.title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria.
journal_articles.abstract: Defense-associated reverse transcriptases (DRTs) employ diverse and distinctive mechanisms of cDNA synthesis to protect bacteria against viral infection1. However, the functions and mechanisms of many DRTs remain unknown2. Here we identify a new antiviral defense system, DRT10, that associates with a noncoding RNA (ncRNA) to catalyze processive, protein-primed synthesis of tandem-repeat DNA. Reverse transcription is templated by a defined ncRNA region with a characteristic sequence pattern and template boundary elements, both of which are conserved and essential for DNA repeat addition. Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal an unanticipated 2:1 architecture, wherein two RT monomers bind opposite sides of a pseudo-symmetric ncRNA. Biochemical experiments further demonstrate that each RT monomer reverse transcribes the template encoded on its respective side of the ncRNA, but only one generates the long repetitive product, whose template is defined by the distance between two flanking stem-loop anchors. This mode of iterative, boundary-delimited cDNA synthesis exhibits direct parallels to the mechanism of telomeric repeat addition by eukaryotic telomerase, and phylogenetic analyses of RTs across domains of life place telomerase in a monophyletic clade with the DRT family, suggesting a common origin for their DNA polymerization activities. Together with earlier studies of DRT2, DRT3, and DRT93-5, our findings identify a conserved mechanistic logic underlying RNA-templated DNA repeat addition across diverse DRTs, despite vastly different architectural solutions, and expand the repertoire of reverse transcription-based strategies for antiviral immunity in bacteria.

journal_articles.title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling.
journal_articles.abstract: Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

journal_articles.title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades.
journal_articles.abstract: In acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, capillary no-reflow denotes that capillary blood flow is still blocked despite successful arterial reperfusion. This is associated with substantially increased mortality and reinfarction risk; nevertheless, no targeted therapy exists so far1,2. Because capillary no-reflow is driven by smooth muscle myosin-mediated hypercontraction of capillary pericytes, we developed R(+)2501, a myosin-specific and capillary-selective vasodilator. In reperfused animal models of acute myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury, direct in vivo imaging showed that R(+)2501 rapidly restored capillary flow, an effect sustained even after rapid drug clearance. Ex vivo experiments confirmed reversal of pericyte constriction directly. Restoration of capillary blood flow, together with clearance of trapped neutrophils, linked resolution of capillary no-reflow to attenuation of an early driver of reperfusion injury. R(+)2501 enhanced capillary perfusion while preserving coronary autoregulation and systemic haemodynamics, and markedly improved survival during acute reperfusion. We further found that acute myocardial infarction induced renal capillary no-reflow, which was reversed by R(+)2501, suggesting that capillary no-reflow contributes to the pathophysiology of cardiorenal syndrome type I. These findings establish pericyte-targeted smooth muscle myosin inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to restore microvascular perfusion and halt the ischaemic cascade across organs, while defining a specific physiological role for capillaries and pericytes in circulatory regulation.

journal_articles.title: Catalytic transfer of carbon atoms enables spirofusion of C-C σ-bonds.
journal_articles.abstract: Spirocyclic frameworks, polycyclic structures in which two rings share a single carbon atom, constitute key structural motifs across diverse areas, including optoelectronic and hole-transporting materials1-3, ligand design for coordination complexes4-6, and numerous natural products7. In a spiro skeleton, the two molecular units adopt an orthogonal arrangement, generating a rigid three-dimensional (3D) architecture. Introducing a single carbon atom to join two components to form the spiro centre therefore represents a direct strategy for constructing such frameworks. Previous carbon-atom-transfer approaches have largely relied on π-bond reactivity, whereas controlled insertion of a carbon atom into C-C σ-bonds remains challenging8-11. Here we report a rhodium-catalysed spiro-carbon-atom insertion reaction that converts biphenylene substrates into spirocyclic structures through sequential C-C bond activation. Using N-isocyanoiminophosphorane (PINC)12-14 as an atomic carbon equivalent, the reaction forms four new C-C bonds at a spiro centre. The transformation enables both homo- and cross-spirofusion of biphenylenes and can be extended to reactions combining σ- and π-bond activation. These results establish a catalytic strategy for constructing structurally complex spirocyclic frameworks through C-C σ-bond activation, with a single carbon atom serving as a central linchpin.

journal_articles.title: Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films.
journal_articles.abstract: Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1-6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7-11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m-3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components.

journal_articles.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K.
journal_articles.abstract: Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition1. Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV-V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

journal_articles.title: De novo design of cysteine proteases.
journal_articles.abstract: Despite advances in de novo enzyme design, success has been largely limited to low-energy-barrier model reactions. Amide bonds such as those linking amino acids along the peptide backbone are stable for hundreds of years in neutral aqueous solution because of the high energy barrier to hydrolysis1. Here we describe the de novo design of enzymes that use an activated cysteine nucleophile to hydrolyse the polypeptide backbone in a sequence-dependent manner, with a success rate of 13/69 = 19% and rate enhancements over the background reaction (kcat/kuncat) of up to 3 × 107. The designed proteases have folds that are very different from proteases in nature (TM score < 0.50), and six crystal structures are very close to the design models (Cα root mean squared deviation of <1.2 Å), highlighting the capacity for generalization and the accuracy of the design methodology. Experimental and computational analyses suggest that the remaining gap in activity to the most active native cysteine proteases arises from imperfections in active-site preorganization and substrate positioning. The designed proteases efficiently cleave their targets in mammalian cells, opening the door to a wide range of synthetic biology applications.

journal_articles.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas.
journal_articles.abstract: Astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas are isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas that most commonly arise in adults under the age of 50 and exhibit variable responses to treatment1-3. To understand the genetic drivers of disease progression, here we used whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing to characterize longitudinally collected tumour specimens from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma. Samples were collected through the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis (GLASS) Consortium4. Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas). We validated known genomic markers of tumour progression, including hypermutation and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A or CDKN2B (hereafter, CDKN2A/B)5, and discovered genetic alterations that distinguish between the evolutionary trajectories of astrocytomas and those of oligodendrogliomas. Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden. In recurrent astrocytomas, however, again irrespective of treatment, acquired focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions were associated with an increase in chromosomal imbalances, which converged with markers of chromosomal instability such as chromothripsis and whole-genome doubling. In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected. Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically. We show that the genomes of oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas adapt to the selective pressures of tumour progression and treatment in distinct ways, suggesting that oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas differ in their responses to treatment-induced DNA damage.

journal_articles.title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue.
journal_articles.abstract: Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column1-3. During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle4-6, giving rise to a neck region. This head-shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats4,5,7-9. However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components10 have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head-shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by Eusthenopteron) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head-shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods11-14, provides a better functional explanation for the head-shoulder separation.

journal_articles.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks.
journal_articles.abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1-7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In 'low-dosage' villages (in which 5-30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50-100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated-treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated-untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals' connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable.

journal_articles.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation.
journal_articles.abstract: Haematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) transplantation-mediated replacement of microglia-the reconstitution of the central nervous system microglial niche with donor-derived myeloid cells-represents a promising strategy for brain cell therapies1-7. However, the cell-intrinsic molecular regulators of HSPC-derived myeloid lineage commitment in the brain have remained largely uncharacterized. This is partially because the scarcity of primary HSPCs has rendered large-scale genetic interrogation intractable. Here we explored whether ex vivo expansion of primary cultured HSPCs (cHSPCs) enables unbiased genetic interrogation of haematopoietic differentiation. We established that cHSPCs can be genetically manipulated and readily differentiate into myeloid cells and repopulate microglia niches of the brain after transplantation. Moreover, primary neonatal astrocytes contained strong signals to induce myeloid specification of cHSPCs in vitro. To identify genes that regulate glia-induced myeloid differentiation, we successfully screened around 20,000 individual genetic perturbations and characterized genes involved in the regulation of cell signalling, cell cycle, mitochondrial function and protein translation. Among these genes was elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (Elp1), which suppressed the unfolded protein response during myeloid specification and was essential for the generation but not maintenance of myeloid cells. Our work establishes a platform to investigate the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid biology.

journal_articles.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism.
journal_articles.abstract: Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities1-5. Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10's potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

journal_articles.title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test.
journal_articles.abstract: Space-based remote sensing allows detection and monitoring of large, concentrated methane sources worldwide1. However, independent evaluation of instruments and algorithms is limited, and new satellites and artificial intelligence techniques have not been tested under controlled, single-blind conditions2. Here we conduct a year-long, single-blind test involving 746 events: 481 methane releases of 9.5-1,183.7 kg h-1 and 265 blank controls. We released metered methane quantities in Arizona, USA, coinciding with overpasses from 12 government, commercial and non-profit satellites. Fifteen analysis teams from nine countries generated more than 2,250 estimates, making this, to our knowledge, the largest controlled test so far and one of the first evaluations of the instruments EMIT, Tanager-1 (Carbon Mapper) and GHOSt. Performance is heterogeneous: 'built-for-purpose' instruments designed to target methane demonstrate excellent detection performance (92-100% true positive rate, 0-11% false positive rate) and quantification accuracy (slope 0.83-1.00, 44% mean absolute percentage error). Instruments repurposed for methane sensing perform more variably (detection rates 62-88%, 46% mean absolute percentage error); still, many demonstrate significant skill. Broad land scanners detect poorly at tested rates but have consistent global coverage and historical archives, motivating additional work. Artificial intelligence-based methods show promise, but caution is warranted; 79% of false positives emerge from these methods. Ground-measured cloud cover >20% degraded performance across systems, raising concerns for use in some locations. Our findings show that satellite-based measurements can achieve accurate detection and quantification of methane point sources when the source location is approximately known.

journal_articles.title: Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes.
journal_articles.abstract: In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1-3. However, elucidation of this structure at an atomic level of detail has been challenging to accomplish via a purely experimental approach. Here we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations4-16, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical data3,17-20 and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without bound anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This insight explains the success of empirically chosen ethylene-carbonate-containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine-learning force-field-based lithium-ion-battery electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed-phase experiments3,21-24, despite being parameterized to only quantum-chemical gas-phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that machine-learning force-field-based models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution.

journal_articles.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates.
journal_articles.abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5-7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks.

journal_articles.title: Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs.
journal_articles.abstract: Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) have emerged as a promising class of solution-processed light-emitting devices, combining high efficiency with facile fabrication1-5. Amino-acid-based molecular additives are widely used to regulate crystallization and suppress defects in perovskite thin films6-8, yet these molecules are chemically reactive in precursor solutions, in which their transformations and products remain poorly understood. Here we resolve and control the hidden solution-phase chemistry of a ubiquitous additive, 5-aminovaleric acid (5AVA), whose solution-phase reactivity has remained unclear6,9-15. We show that 5AVA undergoes competing in situ reactions during precursor preconditioning, yielding two chemically and functionally distinct products: a beneficial organoamidinium zwitterion and a detrimental Lewis-base lactam. By explaining this reaction dichotomy and establishing targeted reaction-pathway control, we selectively use the beneficial species. Direct synthesis and incorporation of the purified zwitterion decouple its intrinsic passivation function from confounding by-products, yielding perovskite films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 97.2% and PeLEDs with a champion external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, alongside a mean peak EQE of 32.8%. Finally, we demonstrate that this reaction-pathway control concept can be extended to further additive chemistries and emission colours, highlighting its potential as a chemistry-driven strategy for rational additive design in PeLEDs.

journal_articles.title: Interhemispheric monsoon dynamics over the past 450,000 years.
journal_articles.abstract: The global monsoon system provides freshwater to much of Earth's biota, including its human population1. The Milankovitch theory predicts changes in Earth's solar insolation over geologic time, and these variations are expected to result in changes to the global monsoon2. Internal climate forcings, such as ice cover and sea surface temperatures, may also affect the system. However, few records of monsoon variability in the Southern Hemisphere over glacial-interglacial cycles exist to test our understanding of the factors that drive variations in the global monsoon. Here we show that monsoons in both the Southern and Northern Hemispheres vary with Milankovitch forcing, and with internal boundary conditions over the past 450,000 years. We present a record of South American Summer Monsoon (SASM) variability, based on speleothem oxygen-isotope data from the Amazon Basin. South American Summer Monsoon variability and that of a major Northern Hemisphere monsoon-that is, the Asian monsoon3,4-have been strikingly out of phase. However, we observe occasional synchronous behaviour in regions impacted by both monsoons. We identify a synchronicity threshold that is exceeded during ten events, including during glacial terminations. Comparison with palaeoclimatic forcing factors during these intervals indicates that greenhouse gas concentrations, cross-equatorial thermal gradients and sea surface temperatures in both the Atlantic and Pacific probably influence these events. This record demonstrates that the global monsoon can reorganize itself, especially during intervals of rapidly changing planetary boundary conditions.

journal_articles.title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic-water interfaces.
journal_articles.abstract: Plastics have become an integral part of our modern society, largely because they are generally regarded as chemically inert under normal circumstances. However, plastics fragmented into microplastics (less than 5 mm in size) have recently raised significant public concerns, and have been detected widely across ecosystems and human tissues with increasing environmental and health risks1-5. Here we show that commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity in water, manifested by the spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species that increases with interfacial hydrophobicity and strongly correlates with interfacial electrostatics. Ab initio calculations support these observations and reveal that hydroxide oxidation becomes energetically more favourable at increasingly hydrophobic microplastic-water interfaces through the combined effects of partial solvation and electrostatics. These interfacial properties and the resulting oxidative chemistry have direct implications for biomolecular adsorption, protein aggregation, and even cellular damage. Together, our findings challenge the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, identify a possibly overlooked mechanism for the detrimental effects of microplastics on health and the environment, and contribute to a fundamental understanding of the structure-activity relationship of interfacial water, which may inform the design of safer and more sustainable plastic materials.

journal_articles.title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans.
journal_articles.abstract: The origin and early diversification of birds remain highly debated in vertebrate evolution. Although estimates of the evolutionary timescales suggest a Jurassic period radiation1,2, a profound scarcity of fossils from this period has hampered how the distinctive bird bauplan was assembled3-5. Selection for powered flight has been viewed as the primary driver of early avialan skeletal modifications3,6,7, attesting to the independent occurrences of aerodynamic features among paravian lineages8. Here we report on the discovery of a Late Jurassic avialan, Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, gen. et sp. nov., from the Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China9. As one of the earliest diverging avialans, Y. yangyuanensis exhibits a striking mosaic of features, combining a mixture of avialan- and troodontid-like cranial characters, paired with derived postcranial traits and a deinonychosaur-like hyperextensible second pedal digit. Phylogenetically informed analyses show that Y. yangyuanensis possesses markedly short forelimbs-a condition present widely among non-avialan theropods. These findings provide strong evidence for a terrestrial, flightless lifestyle of Y. yangyuanensis. Our study demonstrates that evolution works intensively as exemplified by the occurrence of several, divergent ecological pathways being exploited in the initial diversification of birds.

journal_articles.title: Nearly half of reef-building corals face elevated relative risk of extinction.
journal_articles.abstract: Coral reefs are diverse marine ecosystems that provide ecological functions and economic and social benefits across over 100 tropical countries. Warming driven by climate change is a primary threat to coral reefs and is increasing the frequency of global coral bleaching events. Here we reassessed the IUCN Red List status of 892 reef-building coral species, first assessed in 2008 1. Because species-level population trends are unavailable for most reef-building corals, population reductions were inferred using proxies based on global coral cover trends and projected annual severe bleaching under SSP2-4.5, both over three decades, adjusted using trait-based estimates of species vulnerability. Of the 774 species with sufficient data to be assessed, 340 (44%) were classified as threatened under IUCN Red List criteria. Thirty-three species were assessed as Critically Endangered, 251 as Endangered, and 56 as Vulnerable, most due to risk of population reduction associated with projected thermal stress. These findings predate the three hottest years on record and the fourth global coral bleaching event (2023-2025), and the first exceedance for an annual mean of the 1.5oC global warming threshold. The findings reinforce the importance of limiting further warming to maintain coral biodiversity and reef ecosystem function. The Red List assesses the relative extinction risk of species, whereby species are placed in categories of increasing risk by comparing their population size, decline and geographic range against standardised thresholds. The Red List does not predict whether or when a species may go extinct. As the ranges of coral species remain under-surveyed, future assessments would be strengthened by species-level population data and thermal-stress and recovery metrics that better capture range-representative dynamics.

journal_articles.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor.
journal_articles.abstract: Collective behaviour in quantum materials can produce excitations carrying only a fraction of the quantum numbers of their constituents. A notable case occurs in chains of spin-1 units1, in which a topological gap protects the interior of the chain, whereas spin-1/2 states, half the spin of the units that form it, emerge at the ends2. In short chains, these fractional edge spins couple to each other and their topological protection makes them attractive for hybrid spin-superconductor devices. Whether such fractionalization survives the proximity of a superconducting condensate, however, remains an open question. Here we grow molecular Haldane chains of antiferromagnetically coupled spin-1 triangulene units on a proximitized Au(111)/Nb(110) surface and resolve a parity-dependent coupling of their spin-1/2 edge states to the superconductor by scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. Odd-length chains host Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) bound states inside the superconducting gap, originating from a global S = 1 ground state, whereas even-length chains form an S = 0 ground state decoupled from the superconductor. A two-site model attributes this alternation to the sign and strength of inter-edge interactions, independently confirmed by extra-gap spin excitations in tunnelling spectra. Many-body spin excitations of the S = 1 chain are also detected, decoupled from the superconductor by the much larger Haldane gap. The length-tunable coupling of the edge spins to superconductors opens a route towards molecular spin qubits based on π-conjugated carbon architectures.

journal_articles.title: Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation.
journal_articles.abstract: Hydroformylation has been a cornerstone of industrial organometallic catalysis, with regioselectivity being a critical aspect in this process1,2. Present industrial systems use homogeneous Rh-based catalysts with expensive and toxic phosphine-containing ligands, underscoring the need to develop alternative heterogeneous catalysts that could compete with the actual homogeneous ones3. In this direction, atomically dispersed Rh catalysts have been proposed as promising candidates for hydroformylation4,5. However, achieving high regioselectivity at high conversion is still a big challenge. Here subnanometre Rh2O3 clusters are confined inside the channels of the MFI zeolite, which under reaction conditions disrupt into isolated Rh3+ and Rh+ species. Density functional theory (DFT) investigations combined with spectroscopic and catalytic studies demonstrate that Rh3+-mediated hydroformylation is energetically plausibly similar to Rh+, with Rh3+ being intrinsically more selective for hydroformylation and less selective for double-bond isomerization than Rh+. In the coexistence of both Rh3+ and Rh+ species, we demonstrate the possibility to selectively inhibit Rh+ sites through the addition of N-containing molecules such as N-methylpyrrolidine (MP) or 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), which preferentially coordinate to Rh+ inside MFI zeolite channel, thereby suppressing its isomerization function while leaving Rh3+ sites catalytically accessible. This strategy results in a notable enhancement of regioselectivity, with a state-of-the-art reported highest linear to branched aldehydes (l/b) ratio of 817 with 96% undecanal selectivity at 99.8% 1-decene conversion, using NMP as additive.

journal_articles.title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces.
journal_articles.abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3-5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid-liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid-liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C-H bond functionalization at the solid-liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.
